lesson_title: The R6 000 Fridge That Costs R7 296
hook_text: R279 a month sounds fine. Here is what the fridge REALLY costs.
clip_script: Step four, the truth. Add it all up: R600 deposit plus 24 payments of R279, which is R6 696, giving R7 296. The R6 000 fridge cost R7 296. The extra R1 296 is the price of not having the cash today. Not wrong, not a trick — but a price, and now you can see it. The same arithmetic runs any simple-interest loan. Borrow R2 000 at 8 percent for three years: eight percent of 2 000 is 160 a year, three years is R480, pay back R2 480. The only rule to respect is that eight percent goes into the sum as nought comma nought eight — eight hundredths — never as eight.
visual_style: A fridge with a R6 000 tag; a deposit coin drops, then 24 small R279 coins stack up month by month beside it, and a total counter climbs past 6 000 to stop at 7 296 in red with the gap of R1 296 highlighted.
pacing: Steady coin-stacking rhythm, a pause as the counter passes 6 000, punchy reveal of the gap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to price any loan, sale or VAT slip yourself.
